section_summary: This section consists chiefly of State Department filing and cross-reference sheets paired with diplomatic telegrams on Japanese military movements during the 1932 Shanghai conflict and in Manchuria. It traces the staged Japanese evacuation of positions around Shanghai, the restoration of Chinese police and civil control, and negotiations over the armistice and a proposed round-table conference. At the same time, reports describe Japanese reinforcements moving through Harbin and along the Songhua River and Chinese Eastern Railway, where forces associated with Ma Zhanshan and other commanders resisted the Japanese advance.

people.name: Edwin S. Cunningham
people.role: United States Consul General at Shanghai and sender of reports on the Shanghai fighting and evacuation

people.name: Nelson T. Johnson
people.role: United States Minister to China and sender of Legation telegrams

people.name: Mahlon F. Perkins
people.role: United States diplomat at Peiping who forwarded reports for the Minister

people.name: F. P. Lockhart
people.role: United States consular officer at Tientsin

people.name: Dean Acheson
people.role: United States diplomat at Tientsin

people.name: Myers
people.role: United States consular officer at Mukden

people.name: C. C. Brom
people.role: Lieutenant and United States Naval Attaché who reported on Japanese forces

people.name: Colonel Drysdale
people.role: United States military observer and member of the Shanghai Joint Commission

people.name: Robert H. Soule
people.role: Lieutenant who replaced Colonel Drysdale on the Shanghai Joint Commission

people.name: Mamoru Shigemitsu
people.role: Japanese Minister to China and participant in the Shanghai truce negotiations

people.name: Kuo Tai-chi
people.role: Chinese Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs and truce negotiator
variants: Chinese Vice Foreign Minister Kuo Tai Chi

people.name: Jirō Tamon
people.role: Japanese general and divisional commander at Harbin and later Kirin

people.name: General Hirose
people.role: Japanese divisional commander designated to replace General Tamon at Harbin

people.name: Yoda
people.role: Namesake or commander of the Japanese Yoda Brigade transferred toward Harbin

people.name: Ma Zhanshan
people.role: Chinese general opposing Japanese advances in Heilongjiang

people.name: Wang Delin
people.role: Chinese commander whose troops held the railway east of the Mudan River

people.name: Wang Tien-chung
people.role: Commander in Manchuria of a force composed largely of former bandits

people.name: Chang Tsung-ch'ang
people.role: Chinese commander under whom Wang Tien-chung had formerly served

people.name: Lo Wen-kan
people.role: Chinese Foreign Minister who explained and defended the Shanghai peace agreement

people.name: Lieutenant General Kashii
people.role: Japanese lieutenant general who left for Japan in March 1932

people.name: Major General K. Nakamura
people.role: Japanese major general who succeeded Lieutenant General Kashii

people.name: Yoshinori Shirakawa
people.role: Commander-in-chief of the Japanese expeditionary forces at Shanghai

people.name: Sadao Araki
people.role: Japanese War Minister

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese troops landing in the International Settlement
subfiles.about: A filing note refers to Cunningham's telegram reporting a Japanese landing at the wayside wharf in the Shanghai International Settlement.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 50: Japanese troops reported landed inside the International Settlement.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 50: Japanese landing and conditions at Shanghai
subfiles.about: Cunningham reports quiet fronts at Zhabei and Wusong and the landing of about twelve thousand Japanese troops in the International Settlement.
subfiles.summary: Cunningham reports Zhabei and Wusong quiet and about twelve thousand Japanese troops landed at the wayside wharf in the International Settlement.

subfiles.title: File note on Lieutenant Brom's report about Japanese forces
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to a report by Naval Attaché Lieutenant C. C. Brom on Japanese troop movements and equipment.
subfiles.summary: File note on despatch no. 1385 with Lieutenant Brom's observations on the movement and equipment of Japanese forces.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese deployments from Tientsin
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to a Tientsin despatch about Japanese detachments sent to Shanhaiguan and an enlarged garrison at Peiping.
subfiles.summary: File note: small Japanese detachments periodically left Tientsin for Shanhaiguan and the Peiping garrison was increased.

subfiles.title: Despatch extract on Japanese movements near Shanhaiguan
subfiles.about: Lockhart reports Japanese detachments from Tientsin and rumors of operations along the railway between Shanhaiguan and Tanggu.
subfiles.summary: Extract: Japanese troops sent to Shanhaiguan and Peiping came from Tientsin's concession forces; operations along the railway to Tanggu were possible but unconfirmed, says Lockhart.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese and Chinese troop strength
subfiles.about: The sheet records an estimate of about 51,000 Japanese troops in China and uncertainty over Chinese troop dispositions.
subfiles.summary: File note estimating Japanese strength in China at about 51,000, with reliable Chinese figures hard to obtain.

subfiles.title: File note on contemplated Japanese withdrawal from Shanghai
subfiles.about: The sheet notes that the Tokyo War Office was considering withdrawing some troops from Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: File note: Tokyo considered a partial withdrawal from Shanghai, but headquarters had received no order.

subfiles.title: Telegram: Joint situation reports nos. 6 and 7
subfiles.about: Johnson reports stabilization of the Shanghai front and orders for the Eleventh Division and Twenty-fourth Mixed Brigade to return to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Joint reports 6 and 7: the 14th Division entered the line with minor clashes; Tokyo considered withdrawals, and the 11th Division and 24th Mixed Brigade were ordered home.

subfiles.title: File note on the beginning of Japanese withdrawal from Shanghai
subfiles.about: A poorly preserved filing note records an ambassador's statement that withdrawal of Japanese forces from Shanghai had begun.
subfiles.summary: File note: an ambassador believed Japan's withdrawal from Shanghai was under way; source and date illegible.

subfiles.title: File note on Colonel Drysdale's report of an embarkation
subfiles.about: The sheet summarizes Colonel Drysdale's report that a Japanese brigade had begun embarking.
subfiles.summary: File note: Colonel Drysdale reports part of a Japanese brigade embarked March 18, the rest the next day.

subfiles.title: Telegram: Twenty-fourth Mixed Brigade embarking for Moji
subfiles.from: Nelson T. Johnson, forwarding Colonel Drysdale's report
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington, for the War Department
subfiles.about: Drysdale reports that the Twenty-fourth Mixed Brigade was embarking for Moji and would be followed by the Eleventh Division.
subfiles.summary: Shanghai fronts quiet; one and a half battalions of the 24th Mixed Brigade embarked for Moji, the rest next day, the 11th Division later.

subfiles.title: File note on Joint Situation Report no. 11
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to a situation report stating that the embarkation of a Japanese mixed brigade continued.
subfiles.summary: File note on Joint Situation Report no. 11: continuing departure of a Japanese mixed brigade from Shanghai.

subfiles.title: Telegram: Joint Situation Report no. 11
subfiles.about: Johnson reports continued Japanese embarkation and a Chinese protest over Japanese aircraft operating beyond the Shirakawa patrol zone.
subfiles.summary: Joint report no. 11: a Japanese mixed brigade continues embarking; the Nineteenth Route Army protests Japanese flights beyond the patrol zone, with civilian injury claims unverified.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese troop arrivals at Harbin
subfiles.about: The sheet records the arrival at Harbin of five echelons of Japanese troops from the south.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 276: five Japanese troop echelons reached Harbin on February 25.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 276: Japanese reinforcements at Harbin
subfiles.from: Mahlon F. Perkins, forwarding the American Consul General at Harbin
subfiles.about: The Harbin consul reports Japanese troop arrivals and warns of complications with the Soviet Union if they move toward the frontier.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 276: five echelons reached Harbin with more expected; the military seems determined to deploy east despite less serious conditions, risking complications with the Soviet Union.

subfiles.title: File note on Japan's proposed Shanghai truce terms
subfiles.about: The sheet summarizes Japan's position that withdrawal from Shanghai should remain voluntary and outside neutral control.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 362: Japan opposes neutral control over its Shanghai withdrawal.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 362: Japanese objections to the Shanghai truce draft
subfiles.about: Perkins forwards Japanese press reports detailing the government's proposed truce terms and objections to neutral supervision.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 362: Japan wants voluntary withdrawal to the Shanghai-Wusong line, flexible policing and a later round-table conference, and objects to neutral attachés supervising withdrawal and Chinese-only policing.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese troop strength at Tientsin
subfiles.about: The sheet notes that two hundred Japanese troops arrived in Tientsin but that comparable departures left the total garrison unchanged.
subfiles.summary: File note: about two hundred Japanese troops reached Tientsin February 14, but a similar number left, so no substantial net increase, says Lockhart.

subfiles.title: File note on replacement of General Tamon at Harbin
subfiles.about: The sheet reports that General Hirose and his division would replace General Tamon at Harbin.
subfiles.summary: File note: General Tamon's troops at Harbin to be relieved by General Hirose's division.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 444: Change of Japanese divisions at Harbin
subfiles.from: Mahlon F. Perkins, forwarding the American Consul General at Harbin
subfiles.about: The Harbin consul reports the impending replacement of General Tamon and his troops by General Hirose's division.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 444: the American Consul General at Harbin says General Tamon and his troops will soon leave, replaced by General Hirose's division.

subfiles.title: File note on the projected withdrawal from Shanghai
subfiles.about: The sheet records a statement that Japanese troops would leave Shanghai once order was restored, possibly within six months.
subfiles.summary: File note: an undersecretary predicted Japanese withdrawal from Shanghai after order is restored, possibly within six months.

subfiles.title: File note on the Yoda Brigade's movement to Harbin
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to an announcement that the Yoda Brigade had left Changchun for Harbin.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 474: the Yoda Brigade left Changchun northward for Harbin.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 474: Transfer of the Yoda Brigade
subfiles.from: Mahlon F. Perkins, forwarding the American Consul General at Mukden
subfiles.about: The Mukden consul reports that the Yoda Brigade moved from Changchun to Harbin after an earlier transfer from Jinzhou.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 474: the Yoda Brigade left Changchun for Harbin after moving through Tongliao and Siping, replaced at Jinzhou by the Hirosaki Brigade.

subfiles.title: File note on northward Japanese movements in Manchuria
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to confidential information that Japanese troops were moving north in Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: File note on a confidential telegram: substantial Japanese forces moving toward northern Manchuria.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 495: Japanese reinforcements moving north
subfiles.from: Mahlon F. Perkins, forwarding the American Consul General at Mukden
subfiles.about: A confidential Mukden report describes the movement of Japanese divisions and reinforcements into eastern Jilin and northern Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 495: the Korea Division at Jinzhou was relieved by the Hirosaki Division and sent to eastern Jilin; Japan calls northern Manchuria serious and has requested more troops.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese river transport in Manchuria
subfiles.about: The sheet records the movement of Japanese troops down the Songhua River in steamers escorted by gunboats.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 499: armed river transport used in the Japanese advance north of Harbin.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 499: Fighting and Japanese advances north and east of Harbin
subfiles.from: Mahlon F. Perkins, forwarding a Reuters report from Harbin
subfiles.about: A Reuters report describes damaged railways, Japanese advances toward Mudanjiang, river-borne troop movements, and arrests connected with an alleged plot against the Lytton Commission.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 499: anti-Manchukuo troops destroyed Huhai Railway bridges while Japanese advanced toward Mudanjiang and up the Songhua; arrests followed an alleged plot against the Lytton Commission.

subfiles.title: File note on resistance along the Huhai Railway
subfiles.about: The sheet says Heilongjiang troops supporting Ma Zhanshan held the railway north of Hulan against Japanese forces.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 501: Chinese efforts to block a Japanese advance along the Huhai Railway.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 501: Military situation around Harbin
subfiles.from: Mahlon F. Perkins, forwarding the American Consul General at Harbin
subfiles.about: The Harbin consul reports fighting on the Huhai Railway, Songhua River, and Chinese Eastern Railway east of Harbin.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 501: Ma Zhanshan's troops control the Huhai Railway north of Hulan; Japanese entrench near Songpu and advance by steamer, while former Jilin troops occupy Bin County amid railway damage.

subfiles.title: File note on the May 6 withdrawal from Shanghai
subfiles.about: The sheet notes the withdrawal of one Japanese battalion from each of several Shanghai-area positions.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 222: Japanese forces began withdrawing a battalion apiece from designated localities May 6.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 222: First withdrawals of the Third Division
subfiles.about: Cunningham reports Japanese battalions leaving Nanxiang, Luodian, Liuhe, and Jiading for embarkation at Wusong.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 222: one battalion each from Nanxiang, Luodian, Liuhe and Jiading withdrawn to Wusong for Dalian, part of the Third Division's roughly 24,000 men; Chinese police to take over.

subfiles.title: File note on Wang Tien-chung's force in Manchuria
subfiles.about: The sheet describes a Japanese-assisted force in Manchuria under Wang Tien-chung.
subfiles.summary: File note: Wang Tien-chung, ex-officer under Chang Tsung-ch'ang, led mostly former bandits in Manchuria, reportedly organized with Japanese help the previous autumn.

subfiles.title: File note on the completion of the first evacuation phase
subfiles.about: The sheet reports Drysdale's observation of the peaceful evacuation of Luodian and the return of Chinese police.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 235: first evacuation phase ended at Luodian; further withdrawals depend on developments.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 235: Luodian evacuated
subfiles.about: Cunningham reports Drysdale's observation of the Japanese evacuation of Luodian and the scheduled transition to Chinese control.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 235: Colonel Drysdale saw the Japanese evacuate Luodian and Chinese police enter peacefully, completing the first phase; no date set for the next withdrawal.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese unit withdrawals of May 9
subfiles.about: The sheet records the withdrawal of complete Japanese units and anticipates further departures.
subfiles.summary: File note: complete Japanese units withdrew May 9, with more to follow.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 232: Evacuation of Liuhe, Jiading, Nanxiang, and Luodian
subfiles.about: Cunningham details the transfer of evacuated towns to Chinese police and civil administrators under the May 5 agreement.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 232: complete Japanese units left Liuhe, Jiading and Nanxiang and Luodian is to be evacuated May 10; 400 Nanking special police are ready, and Cunningham asks how much detail to report.

subfiles.title: File note on completion of the Japanese army evacuation
subfiles.about: The sheet records the evacuation of Jiangwan, restoration of Chinese control, and embarkation of the last Japanese army units.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 273: Chinese authorities resumed control of Jiangwan May 29 and the last Japanese army units embarked May 31.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 273: Final army embarkations and remaining naval forces
subfiles.about: Cunningham reports completion of the army evacuation while Japanese naval forces and gendarmes retained several Shanghai positions.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 273: the army's last units left, but Japanese naval forces kept the Wusong barracks, Yinghsiang and Zhabei; Chinese gendarmes reoccupied Longhua.

subfiles.title: File note on the May 9 evacuation of three towns
subfiles.about: The sheet reports complete Japanese evacuation of Liuhe, Jiading, and Nanxiang and the restoration of Chinese control.
subfiles.summary: File note: a War Department report says the May 9 transfer of three localities to Chinese control occurred without trouble.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 233: Drysdale's report on the first evacuation line
subfiles.from: Edwin S. Cunningham, forwarding Colonel Drysdale's report
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington, for the War Department
subfiles.about: Drysdale reports the evacuation of Liuhe, Jiading, and Nanxiang and the planned evacuation of Luodian.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 233: Drysdale reports Japanese forces fully evacuated Liuhe, Jiading and Nanxiang, Luodian next, leaving a line through Yinghsiang, Dachang and Zhenru; the 14th Division goes to Manchuria.

subfiles.title: File note on Lo Wen-kan's statement about the peace agreement
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to Lo Wen-kan's expression of confidence that Japanese troops would withdraw from Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 511: Chinese Foreign Minister Lo expects Japanese troops to return to pre-January 28 positions.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 511: Lo Wen-kan explains the Shanghai agreement
subfiles.from: Mahlon F. Perkins, forwarding a Kuo Wen report from Nanking
subfiles.about: Lo Wen-kan defends the Shanghai peace settlement and discusses its implications for Manchuria and relations with the Soviet Union.
subfiles.summary: Lo says Chinese negotiators defeated demands for a round-table, free port and boycott suppression; the agreement is the best available, China will next address Manchuria, and Soviet actions hinder relations.

subfiles.title: File note on a change in Japanese command at Tientsin
subfiles.about: The sheet reports Kashii's departure, Nakamura's succession, and growing Japanese opposition to military operations at Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: File note: Lt. Gen. Kashii left Tientsin March 10, succeeded by Major General Nakamura, with growing opposition in Japan to the Shanghai campaign.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese activity at Shanhaiguan
subfiles.about: The sheet says reported Japanese military activity at Shanhaiguan consisted of minor maneuvers and that the garrison had not increased.
subfiles.summary: File note: Japan's Shanhaiguan garrison is about two hundred, and recent actions were demonstrations, not a major buildup.

subfiles.title: Telegram: Japanese and Manchukuo actions at Shanhaiguan
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington, and American Legation in China
subfiles.about: Acheson reports demonstrations by the Japanese garrison and the brief occupation of Shanhaiguan station by Manchukuo police.
subfiles.summary: Japanese officials call Shanhaiguan activity minor and the garrison not reinforced; one hundred Manchukuo police under a Japanese officer occupied the station and withdrew after a British railway official protested.

subfiles.title: File note on the cabinet decision to evacuate Shanghai
subfiles.about: The sheet records a Reuters report that Japan would withdraw its expeditionary force from Shanghai within a month.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 524: only a small bluejacket force will remain to protect Japanese residents after the army leaves Shanghai.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 524: Japanese cabinet orders complete Shanghai withdrawal
subfiles.from: Nelson T. Johnson, forwarding a Reuters report from Tokyo
subfiles.about: A Japanese Foreign Office spokesman announces the withdrawal of the Shanghai expeditionary force and the retention of only a small naval guard.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 524: Japan's cabinet orders the entire expeditionary force withdrawn within a month, leaving only a small bluejacket force; the spokesman cites world opinion but warns other powers bear responsibility.

subfiles.title: File note on the Utsunomiya Division's movement north
subfiles.about: The sheet records the movement of Utsunomiya Division troops from Dalian through Harbin toward Sanxing.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 527: transfer north of Japanese troops formerly at Shanghai.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 527: Utsunomiya Division deployed against bandits
subfiles.from: Nelson T. Johnson, forwarding the American Consul General at Mukden
subfiles.about: The Mukden consul reports the movement of Utsunomiya Division troops to Sanxing for a major campaign in northern Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 527: Utsunomiya Division troops move from Dalian via Harbin to Sanxing for a campaign against bandits before crops grow, and the South Manchuria Railway suspends commercial freight.

subfiles.title: File note on Joint Commission notice of full withdrawal
subfiles.about: The sheet records the Japanese delegation's statement that the entire army would leave Shanghai within about a month.
subfiles.summary: The filing note refers to telegram no. 240. It summarizes an oral notice delivered through the Sino-Japanese Joint Commission.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 240: Japanese delegation promises withdrawal by June 10
subfiles.about: Cunningham reports an official oral assurance that the Japanese army would leave the Shanghai area by about June 10.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 240: the Japanese delegation orally told the Chinese the whole Shanghai army would be withdrawn within about a month, by June 10 at the latest.

subfiles.title: File note on Chinese conditions for a round-table conference
subfiles.about: The sheet says China would not attend a Shanghai round-table conference until Japanese forces withdrew in Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 529: China demands Japanese troops first retire into Manchuria's railway zone before a round-table conference.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 529: Chinese position on broader negotiations
subfiles.from: Nelson T. Johnson, forwarding Reuters reports
subfiles.about: Reuters reports that China viewed the Shanghai armistice as only a partial settlement and would not negotiate political issues while Japanese troops occupied Chinese territory.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 529: no Shanghai round-table until Japanese troops leave Manchuria for the railway zone; Shanghai expects withdrawal around May 20 and General Shirakawa's relief.

subfiles.title: File note on Imperial authority over Japanese army movements
subfiles.about: The sheet records the Japanese position that an Imperial withdrawal order could not be countermanded.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 530: army movements are decided by Imperial authority, not Shanghai residents' petitions.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 530: Araki on the Shanghai withdrawal order
subfiles.from: Nelson T. Johnson, forwarding a Rengo report from Tokyo
subfiles.about: War Minister Araki says the withdrawal order is irrevocable and reports military deliberations on policy after the evacuation.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 530: Araki tells Shanghai residents the withdrawal order cannot be rescinded but the army won't abandon them; the Supreme Military Council considered post-withdrawal policy.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese troop movements in Manchuria
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to a report on continuing Japanese troop movements through Harbin.
subfiles.summary: The filing note points to telegram no. 531. Its subject is the deployment of Japanese reinforcements in northern Manchuria.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 531: Japanese advance from Harbin
subfiles.from: Nelson T. Johnson, forwarding the American Consul General at Harbin
subfiles.about: The Harbin consul reports Japanese forces moving east and down the Songhua River while Ma Zhanshan threatens the western railway line.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 531: Japanese troops arriving from the south go east along the Chinese Eastern Railway or down the Songhua, while Ma Zhanshan's fortified troops threaten the line near Anda.

subfiles.title: File note on the withdrawal of Japanese bluejackets
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to Drysdale's observation of Japanese bluejackets leaving an evacuated Shanghai district.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 245: Japanese naval personnel withdrew and Chinese police peacefully resumed control.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 245: Chinese police resume control south of the railway
subfiles.about: Cunningham reports the withdrawal of Japanese bluejackets and Drysdale's replacement by Lieutenant Soule on the Joint Commission.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 245: Drysdale saw bluejackets leave Zhabei south of the railway and 500 Peiping police take over; Lt. Soule replaces him on the Joint Commission.

subfiles.title: File note on the scheduled evacuation of Dachang
subfiles.about: The sheet says Dachang would be evacuated on May 17 and notes Chinese requests concerning railway repairs.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 246: next Japanese withdrawal from Dachang and Chinese efforts to regain railway lines.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 246: Arrangements for the Dachang evacuation
subfiles.about: Cunningham reports Japanese notice of the Dachang evacuation and Chinese preparations to take over the area and railway lines.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 246: the Japanese will evacuate Dachang at one o'clock May 17; China names personnel to restore control and asks that railway lines also be evacuated.

subfiles.title: File note on the Japanese withdrawal from Dachang
subfiles.about: The sheet records the withdrawal of Japanese infantry from Dachang and the return of Chinese police.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 247: Chinese police peacefully resumed control after the Japanese battalion left Dachang.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 247: Lieutenant Soule observes the Dachang transfer
subfiles.about: Cunningham reports Soule's observation of a Japanese battalion leaving Dachang and Chinese police entering the district.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 247: Lt. Soule saw one Japanese battalion leave Dachang and 150 Nanking police resume control without incident.

subfiles.title: File note on the scheduled withdrawal from Zhenru
subfiles.about: The sheet records Japanese notice that the defense units at Zhenru would withdraw on May 20.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 248: Zhenru and its station are the next positions scheduled for evacuation.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 248: Notice of the Zhenru evacuation
subfiles.about: Cunningham reports that Japanese Joint Commissioners scheduled withdrawal from Zhenru and Zhenru station for May 20.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 248: Japanese commission members notified the Chinese that defense units at Zhenru and its station would leave at one o'clock on May 20.

subfiles.title: File note on revised evacuation plans for Zhenru, Jiangwan, and Zhabei
subfiles.about: The sheet records the postponement of the Zhenru withdrawal and outlines planned withdrawals from Jiangwan and Zhabei.
subfiles.summary: File note on telegram no. 249: Zhenru evacuation deferred to May 23, with further army and naval withdrawals coordinated.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 249: Revised Shanghai evacuation schedule
subfiles.about: Cunningham reports revised dates for withdrawals from Zhenru, Jiangwan, and Zhabei and discusses policing and railway arrangements.
subfiles.summary: Telegram no. 249: Japan postpones Zhenru's evacuation to May 23, plans to leave western Jiangwan May 19 and most of Zhabei May 23, and complains Dachang was not taken over by special police.

subfiles.title: File note on the withdrawal from Jiangwan
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to Lieutenant Soule's observation of the Japanese withdrawal from Jiangwan and the return of Chinese police control.
subfiles.summary: File note: Lt. Soule witnessed Japanese forces leave Jiangwan and Chinese police resume authority; the telegram continues beyond this section.
